title: Asking, telling, and forbidding
title_target: একটু বসুন, চা খেয়ে যান — èk-Tu bô-sun, cha khé-yé jan
goal: Tell and ask people at three levels of politeness, and forbid with a না at the end — including one gentle form that looks like the future but is really a request.
bekal: forming commands for আপনি, তুমি, and তুই
forbidding with করবেন না, করো না
softening requests with একটু and না
using the -বেন form as the politest request

dialogs.title: কথোপকথন — A guest drops by unannounced
dialogs.intro: A neighbor, Rina, drops in for a visit. The whole dialog is full of commands — but notice that almost all of them are hospitality, not orders.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: Rina! Come in, come in. Sit here.
lines.literal: Rina — sister! come, come. sit — here.

lines.speaker: রিনা:
lines.id: No, no, I won't stay long. I have things to do.
lines.literal: no — no, long — will-stay — not. business — is-there.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: At least have some tea first. Ani, could you bring some water?
lines.literal: at-least — tea — drink-then — go. Ani, a-little — water — will-give?

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Of course. Rina, cold or hot?

lines.speaker: রিনা:
lines.id: Just cold. And listen, no sugar, please.
lines.literal: cold-just — give. and — listen, sugar — give — don't.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: Rina is diabetic. Ani, make it without sugar.
lines.literal: sister — diabetes. Ani, sugar — without — will-make.

lines.speaker: রিনা:
lines.id: Please don't go to any trouble. I just came to see you.
lines.literal: you-all — busy — become — don't. I — only — see-to — have-come.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: It's no trouble at all. Just a moment.
lines.literal: at-all — busy — am-being — not. a-little — wait — do.

lines.speaker: রিনা:
lines.id: Ani, how are you? Try speaking a little Bengali!
lines.literal: Ani, you — how — are? Bengali — speak — [na] — a-little!

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: I'm fine. Please speak slowly, then I'll understand.
lines.literal: I — well — am, sister. slowly — will-say, then — will-understand.

lines.speaker: রিনা:
lines.id: Wow! Wonderful! Don't be scared, you can do it.
lines.literal: wow! wonderful! fear — get — don't, you — will-be-able.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: Here's the tea. Drink it while it's hot!
lines.literal: here — take — tea. hot — hot — eat!

notes: **Commands have three levels, matching the three words for “you”.** For **আপনি**, the ending is **-উন**: করুন, বলুন, বসুন, শুনুন — the form to use with everyone at first. For **তুমি**, the ending is **-ও**: করো, বলো, বসো, শোনো. For **তুই**, the bare stem with no ending: কর, বল, বস, শোন.

⚠️ **A few আপনি commands are irregular and very common:** যাওয়া → **যান** (not *যাউন*), আসা → **আসুন**, খাওয়া → **খান**, দেওয়া → **দিন**, নেওয়া → **নিন**, হওয়া → **হন**. These six cover most everyday talk; learn them together.

**There's a fourth, even politer form, and it looks like the future: -বেন.** আস্তে **বলবেন** (please speak slowly), একটু **দেবেন**? (could you give me…?), **আসবেন** কিন্তু! (do come!). Literally “you will say”, but it means a gentle, unhurried request. ⚠️ It's the safest form for asking strangers for something.

**Forbidding works by putting না at the end, just like negation.** করবেন না (don't do it), যাবেন না (don't go), চিন্তা করবেন না (don't worry), ভয় পাবেন না (don't be afraid). ⚠️ Polite “don't” uses the **-বেন** form, not the -উন command: *করুন না* actually means “go on, do it” — the exact opposite of what you meant.

⚠️ **So না after a command can mean two opposite things, and the verb form decides.** **করবেন না** (-বেন form) = don't do it. **করুন না** (-উন form) = go on, do it. The key is the verb form, not the না.

**একটু softens almost any request.** একটু বসুন (sit down a moment), একটু দেখুন (take a look), একটু সরুন (move over a bit), একটু অপেক্ষা করুন (wait a moment). ⚠️ Without একটু, a command sounds like an instruction; with একটু, it becomes a request — much like *just* or *a moment* in English.

**Declining an offer in a Bengali home has its own etiquette.** Declining once is politeness; the host will offer again. A phrase that works: **সত্যিই লাগবে না, ধন্যবাদ** (I really don't need it, thank you). ⚠️ But once the tea is poured, accept it — refusing then feels like rejecting the person, not the drink. And **চা খেয়ে যান** (have some tea before you go) is one you should accept at least once.

grammars.title: Three levels of command
after: **The gentle -বেন request is used for things that aren't urgent and for wishes that apply later:** আসবেন (do come), লিখে দেবেন (please write it down for me later), ভালো থাকবেন (take care). ⚠️ Note that **ভালো থাকবেন** — the warmest goodbye — is actually this gentle command form.

grammars.title: The most common requests
after: ⚠️ **দয়া করে sounds very formal and is rare in everyday talk.** For ordinary requests, একটু is more than enough and sounds far more natural. Save দয়া করে for letters, announcements, and earnest pleas.

blocks.title: ⚠️ On giving and getting commands
items: **Bengali commands sound much friendlier than their translations.** আসুন, বসুন, খান — this string of commands is a host's hospitality, not orders. Don't be offended by them, and don't be shy about using them.
**Adults use তুমি or তুই with small children**, and that's normal. But if someone uses তুই with **you** and you aren't close, it's a sign of disrespect — though often unintended by older people.

**If you're asked to speak Bengali in front of a group**, like Ani in this dialog, just answer with one sentence you know well. A short correct sentence impresses far more than a long messy one — and people will clap for both.

blocks.text: An expression worth keeping: **গরম গরম খান** — “eat it while it's hot”. Bengali often repeats an adjective to stress the state: গরম গরম (piping hot), তাজা তাজা (nice and fresh), আস্তে আস্তে (slowly, little by little), তাড়াতাড়ি (quickly, from তাড়া). ⚠️ English does something similar with *nice and hot* or *slowly but surely*, but Bengali doubles the word itself.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: বসুন — যান — খান — দিন — শুনুন — আসুন
চিন্তা করবেন না। — যাবেন না। — ভয় পাবেন না। — এখানে বসবেন না।
একটু অপেক্ষা করুন। — চিন্তা করবেন না। — চা খেয়ে যান। — একটু লিখে দেবেন। — গরম গরম খান।
একটু বসুন। — আস্তে বলুন। — চিন্তা করবেন না। — একটু অপেক্ষা করুন। — আর লাগবে না, ধন্যবাদ। — আজ পারব না, দুঃখিত।
